Required action: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines. Due date: 2026-11-26. Known ransomware use: Unknown.

1.title: GHSA-2v9w-34q6-wpqx — jline3 leads to ReDoS in Built-in Less Viewer Search
1.summary:
### Summary

The JLine3 built-in `less` pager compiles user-supplied search patterns directly as
Java regular expressions with no sanitization, timeout, or backtracking bound. A
malicious pattern such as `(a+)+b` can trigger catastrophic backtracking and hang the
session thread at 100% CPU. In deployments that expose `less` over Telnet or SSH,
this becomes a denial-of-service issue for the affected session and can be used to
exhaust a bounded session pool.

1.summary:
## Summary

2.title: New UX Arrives to Change Meeting Organizers
2.summary: In August 2026, Microsoft published news of the new Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer cmdlet to change meeting organizers. Now Outlook and the Teams calendar app get the UX wrapped around the cmdlet to make the feature more accessible to end users. Despite the confusing description of various phases from Microsoft, what’s clear is that they are shipping a feature to partially handle meetings with associated Teams online meetings. More work is needed to deal with meeting artifacts, like attachments. Apparently, phase 3 will fix everything!
